WORKLOG - cafe_contract_desk / task 1 (Ellerbeck Medical Partners, Cambridge dining commons).

STEP 0 - DRAW. `.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0013_workplace_dining_and_catering_provider/tasks/cafe_contract_desk --tasks 2` printed for task 1: {"task": 1, "key": "env_0013_workplace_dining_and_catering_provider/cafe_contract_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 5]}. The tree therefore carries exactly 3 prerequisite problems besides the root, and the four computations carry 6, 4, 4 and 5 declared factors. Assignment chosen by the author: cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment takes 6, cafe_ext_late_charge_assessment takes 4, cafe_ext_early_exit_charge takes 4, cafe_ext_standby_charge_assessment takes 5 - the multiset {4,4,5,6} matches the draw.

STEP 0 - SCOPE. Task 0 occupied cafe_ext_model_change_confirmation, cafe_ext_management_fee_invoice and cafe_ext_service_credit_settlement with the tools confirm_service_model_change_fa28a84a, raise_management_fee_invoice_00d6d0cf and issue_service_credit_9f99d1a6, that is the service model change, the management fee invoice and the service credit. Task 1 claims what was left on the charge and wind-down side: cafe_ext_late_charge_assessment, cafe_ext_early_exit_charge and cafe_ext_standby_charge_assessment on cafe_penalty_fee_posted, and cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment on cafe_invoice_payment_posted, with the four tools post_late_charge_719c9a63, post_early_exit_charge_dadd74c6, post_standby_charge_21704194 and settle_contract_balance_f9be2425. No policy, tool or write subject is shared with task 0, and with two tasks the difficulty is closed: the seven extended policies are covered exactly once between them.

STEP 0 - DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal: a facilities and accounts manager rings to settle her cafe account in full on the day, the site being wound down after written notice given last October. Scored core parameter: the closing settlement, 150431.90 USD. The policy makes that figure wait on three charges that do not yet stand on the contract: the late charge owed on invoicing that has run unpaid, the early exit charge due on the contract ending ahead of its term, and the standby charge owed for the months the counter stood shut. Each is a separate problem with its own multi-factor calculation, and each raises the unsettled balance the settlement reads. Depth: one hop from the root, but three edges wide, and the root's own six factors then read the balance those three writes produced, the contract's records and the client's micro market in another difficulty. Breadth: the four computations between them read eight different aggregates over the cafe ledger across four windows, four aggregates over the service request log, the contract's term dates, first service day, notice day, reported headcount, suspended days and both balances, and the client's micro market agreement with its settlement invoices and subsidy funding lots.

STEP 0 - BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
* cafe_penalty_fee_posted (all three prerequisite writes) is governed by two base policies at once.
  cafe_invoice_payment_terms.chargeable_state: condition "A late charge is only raised while the contract stands in mobilizing, active, suspended or in_transition_out, and never on a closed contract, where the balance is pursued as a closed account instead." The contract stands in_transition_out, inside the allowed set. Negative case: had the contract already closed, no contractual charge could be raised on it at all and the balance would be pursued as a closed account.
  cafe_participation_guarantee.shortfall_state: condition "A shortfall charge is only raised while the contract stands active, suspended or in transition out, and it is never raised in the first three billing periods of a contract because the measurement window is not yet complete." The contract stands in_transition_out and has been serving since 2024-08-19, far beyond its first three billing periods. Negative case: on a contract three months old no contractual charge of this family could be raised.
  Both gates take their evidence from the contract row and bind cafe_contracts.cafe_contract_id to the cafe_contract_id argument of each write.
* cafe_invoice_payment_posted (the root) is governed by cafe_invoice_payment_terms alone, through the same chargeable_state gate, satisfied on the same evidence.
* There is no time eligibility on any of this task's write subjects, so temporal_feasibility is empty; every deadline in play - the 120 day termination notice, the 10 day late charge grace, the 14 day resumption notice - enters the arithmetic as a factor rather than as a base gate, and each is read from the records at frozen_time.

STEP 0 - BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target object: the single Culinary Center Cafe contract at site CS-136, the only cafe contract this client has ever held. Correlation key: cafe_contracts.cafe_contract_id, carried by every one of the four writes. Rows included in an aggregate: the cafe ledger rows carrying that contract id, narrowed by charge code and by the window each ladder names. Rows excluded and why: the 42,000.00 opening project fee of 2024-05-20 is charge code mobilization_fee and enters no management fee aggregate though it is the largest posting on the ledger; the 2025-03-08 management fee of 17,400.00, the 2025-02-14 payment of 17,400.00 and the 2025-02-24 funding lot of 22,000.00 all fall twelve whole months or more back and drop out of every twelve month window; the two standby charges of 2025-06-30 and 2025-07-31 and the two late charges of 2025-07-22 and 2025-11-25 settle the earlier pause and the earlier arrears and are not the charges this call raises, though the late charges are exactly what the arrears rate ladder counts; the declined suspension request of 2025-10-02 is not an approved one and enters no count. On the market side the 2025-12-18 settlement payment and the pre-window settlement invoice of 2025-02-25 are excluded by charge code and by window respectively.

STEP 0 - PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Root: cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment. Prerequisites: cafe_ext_late_charge_assessment, cafe_ext_early_exit_charge and cafe_ext_standby_charge_assessment. Shape: a fan-out of three parallel edges, all value_input, all on the binding unsettled_balance_usd.
Edge 1 - root <- cafe_ext_late_charge_assessment. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the root's own rule: "The closing settlement is fixed only after the late charge owed on the contract's overdue invoice stands on its ledger." Four-point test: (1) the connective "only after" joins the root's own result, the closing settlement, to what it waits on; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state - a late charge standing on the contract's ledger - naming no action, no performer and no tool; (3) no tool, policy id or code token; (4) a hard requirement, scoped to the late charge owed on the overdue invoice and no wider. The direction is the affirmative one because that is how the desk states a charge that rests on something being complete. Exactly one write of this difficulty puts a late charge on a cafe ledger.
Edge 2 - root <- cafe_ext_early_exit_charge. Prerequisite sentence: "Before the closing settlement is worked out, the early exit charge due on the contract ending ahead of its term must stand recorded against the contract." Same four points, affirmative direction, state form, and exactly one write of this difficulty records an early exit charge.
Edge 3 - root <- cafe_ext_standby_charge_assessment. Prerequisite sentence: "The closing settlement is not worked out until the standby charge owed for the months the cafe has stood suspended stands on the contract's ledger." Negated direction, which is how a desk states a settlement that is withheld until something stands; it rewrites exactly into "the closing settlement is worked out only once the standby charge owed for the months the cafe has stood suspended stands on the contract's ledger" with nothing added, dropped or split. State form, and exactly one write of this difficulty puts a standby charge on a cafe ledger. Across the two tasks the charter therefore carries both directions rather than one throughout.
Derivation a reader performs on each edge: the sentence names a kind of entry that must stand on the ledger; the ledger at frozen_time carries no such entry for the current period; the rule of the policy that books that kind of entry says what it books and that it is the write that books it; therefore that problem must be resolved first. Handling-time conditions and the seed evidence that each is false at the opening are recorded in prerequisite_closure. Resolving actions: post_late_charge_719c9a63, post_early_exit_charge_dadd74c6 and post_standby_charge_21704194, all owner agent; the root itself is the client's own write through settle_contract_balance_f9be2425.
Order: the three prerequisites are parallel and may be taken in any order. That is not an assumption: the six orders of the three writes were replayed against the seeded database with the real tools and every one produced the same terminal hash, because the row id of each posting is a content hash of its own arguments and none of the three computations reads a quantity another of them writes - the late charge reads management fee, payment, service credit and late charge postings, the early exit charge reads management fee postings, approved resumption requests and the client's market, and the standby charge reads suspension and resumption requests and management fee postings. None reads the unsettled balance; only the root does. The root is last in every case.
The tool layer blocks nothing: each of the four tools reads the contract row only to copy its customer_id and site_code onto the posting, then writes unconditionally and returns a receipt whatever else does or does not stand on the ledger.

STEP 1 - POLICIES. cafe_ext_late_charge_assessment inherits cafe_invoice_payment_terms and cafe_participation_guarantee and declares two overwrites on cafe_invoice_payment_terms: the clause fixing the late charge to the monthly percentage on the amount still outstanding, and the clause on how a part payment leaves a remainder. cafe_ext_early_exit_charge inherits the same two plus cafe_termination_terms as the lineage its formula reads, and declares two overwrites on cafe_termination_terms: the early exit charge clause and the clause on no charge falling due where the term has run. cafe_ext_standby_charge_assessment inherits the same two plus cafe_service_suspension_terms, and declares two overwrites on cafe_service_suspension_terms: the standby charge clause and the clause on resuming sooner than the notice allows. cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment inherits cafe_invoice_payment_terms and cafe_termination_terms and declares one overwrite on each: the closure settlement clause and the clause on a payment larger than the invoiced amount. All three prerequisite policies are state_due - at month-end reconciliation a contract carrying unpaid invoicing, a pause not yet charged and an exit ahead of term owes each of those charges whether or not anyone rings. The root is on_request: nobody owes a closing settlement until the client asks to pay one, and this client asks in terms.

STEP 1 - FACTOR CARD (tier taken, evidence, and the figure the baseline gives, all from the Step 5 sensitivity run).
cafe_ext_late_charge_assessment, result 678.08, baseline as a whole 0.00.
  outstanding_amount_basis (method): a service credit stands allowed inside twelve months and payments of 74,196.00 fall short of the 125,976.00 of management fees invoiced, so the amount still outstanding is 125,976.00 less 74,196.00 less the 9,400.00 of credits, that is 42,380.00. Baseline, fees less payments only: 51,780.00 and a result of 828.48.
  overdue_clock_anchor (method): a payment stands inside three months (2026-02-20) and a service credit stands inside them too (2025-12-25), so the clock runs from the day after the credit, giving 75 days. Baseline, from the day after the 2026-02-08 invoice: 30 days, one month fewer charged, and a result of 0.00.
  grace_days_band (parameter): two service credits stand allowed inside twelve months and a notice day of 2025-10-20 stands on the contract, so the disputed account grace of 21 days applies and one month is charged. Baseline, the 10 day grace printed against Culinary Center Cafe: two months charged and a result of 1356.16.
  arrears_rate_band (parameter): two late charges stand inside twenty-four months (2025-07-22 and 2025-11-25) and 42,380.00 reaches the 30,000.00 heavy arrears threshold, so the repeat arrears rate of 1.60 per cent applies. Baseline, the 1.00 per cent printed against the model: 423.80.
cafe_ext_early_exit_charge, result 55283.28, baseline as a whole 69600.00.
  unrun_term_exit_months (parameter): 42 whole months of the term stood unrun on the 2025-10-20 notice day and the cafe has been serving 18 whole months, fewer than twenty-four, so 5 months are charged. Baseline, the 4 printed against the model: 44226.62.
  exit_fee_base_band (parameter): five management fee invoices stand inside six months and the highest management fee ever invoiced on the contract, 18,096.00, stands above the 17,400.00 printed against the model, so the base is 18,096.00. Baseline, the printed 17,400.00: 53157.00.
  notice_relief_basis (method): 141 calendar days of notice have run against the 120 printed against the model and two resumption requests stand approved, so the 21 days of notice beyond it are counted in whole weeks - 3 of them, the part week left unrelieved - and one fiftieth of the charge rounded to the nearest cent is relieved for each, that is 1,809.60 a week and 5,428.80 in all. Baseline, no relief at all: 58812.00. What the tiers select is the accrual unit, not a rate: a client who paused and resumed is credited in whole weeks of notice, while a client who never resumed has the same excess counted in calendar days at one three hundred and fiftieth of the charge for each. Strip the fractions out of the two tier sentences and the procedures still differ - count whole weeks and discard the remainder, or count every calendar day - which is the same test applied to task 0's short notice ladder in the same change.
  continuing_outlet_allowance (parameter, cross_difficulty market): the client's micro market stands active and its settlement invoices over twelve months total 91,200.00, at or above the 90,000.00 continuing outlet threshold, so 35.00 per cent is allowed. The tier rests on initial_state.market_agreements status active and the twelve monthly market_ledger settlement invoices of 7,600.00. Baseline, the nil rate: 85051.20. Near-miss: the 2025-02-25 settlement invoice falls twelve whole months back and is outside the window, and the 2025-12-18 settlement payment is excluded by charge code.
cafe_ext_standby_charge_assessment, result 26058.24, baseline as a whole 13920.00.
  suspended_day_count_basis (method): a resumption request stands approved and the day it asked service to return, 2025-09-28, falls after the day the latest approved suspension asked service to stop, 2025-08-16, so the days counted are the 44 calendar days between them with both days counted. Baseline, the 74 suspended days standing against the contract year: 39087.36.
  pause_month_count_basis (method): two suspension requests stand approved and 44 days exceed the 14 day shortest suspension printed against the model, so every whole thirty days is a month and the part beyond is a further month, giving 2. Baseline, which is also the ladder's fall-through and what baseline.rule states - the days divided by thirty and rounded down with a minimum of one: 1 month and 13029.12. A pause not exceeding the shortest suspension now earns no month of pause at all, which is what the inherited base sentence "a pause shorter than the minimum suspension printed against the service model is handled as ordinary closed days rather than as a suspension" says.
  standby_rate_band (parameter): a notice day stands and 44 days reach half the 75 day contract year ceiling, so the wind-down standby rate of 60.00 per cent applies. Baseline, the 40.00 per cent printed against the model: 17372.16.
  standby_fee_base_band (parameter): two management fee invoices stand inside three months and the most recent, 18,096.00, stands at or above the 17,400.00 printed against the model, so the base is their mean of 18,096.00. Baseline, the printed fee: 25056.00.
  late_resumption_loading_band (parameter): the approved resumption was logged on 2025-09-18 for a return on 2025-09-28, 10 days against the 14 day resumption notice printed against the model, and two suspension requests stand approved, so the repeated short resumption loading of 20.00 per cent is added. Baseline, no loading: 21715.20.
cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment, result 150431.90, baseline as a whole 47026.00.
  contract_year_anchor (method): a first service day of 2024-08-19 is recorded and falls 105 calendar days after the 2024-05-06 start of term, more than sixty, so the contract year elapsed is the 18 months of service reduced by whole years, that is 6. Baseline, which is also the ladder's fall-through and word for word what baseline.rule states - the 22 months of term reduced by whole years, that is 10 - leaving 2 whole months of the contract year still to run: 152565.23. No tier of the ladder can make the months still to run negative: the remaining tier, for a contract with no first service day recorded, puts the contract year elapsed at nil.
  equipment_deposit_return_band (parameter): three contractual charges stand raised inside three months - the late charge, the early exit charge and the standby charge this consultation books - and a notice day stands, so 40.00 per cent of the 68,000.00 deposit is returned. Baseline, the whole deposit: 109631.90.
  drawable_funding_refund_basis (method): two funding lots stand inside twelve months (24,000.00 and 21,500.00) and the 69.20 drawn over them falls short, so the refund is 45,430.80. Baseline, the 67,413.60 subsidy funding balance standing on the contract: 144936.20.
  opening_inventory_recovery_band (parameter): the cafe has been serving 18 whole months, twelve or more but fewer than twenty-four, and a notice day stands, so half the 19,500.00 opening inventory is recovered. Baseline, nil recovery: 140681.90.
  outlet_carry_over_band (parameter, cross_difficulty market): the client's micro market stands active and the subsidy funded at its kiosk over twelve months totals 32,500.00, at or above the 26,000.00 carry-over threshold, so 75.00 per cent of the refund is carried over to the market rather than paid back. The tier rests on initial_state.market_agreements status active and the two market_ledger subsidy funding lots of 18,000.00 and 14,500.00. Baseline, nothing carried over: 116358.80.
  smallwares_credit_band (parameter): 74 suspended calendar days stand against the contract year, ten or more, and a notice day stands, so the smallwares share is one half. The rule states the pro-ration the compute performs: the 12,800.00 allowance taken at that share and then reduced to the proportion the 6 whole months of the contract year still to run bear to twelve gives 3,200.00. Baseline, a nil smallwares share: 153631.90.
Across the task every one of the nineteen factors is multi-source except the outstanding amount basis, the arrears rate band and the pause month count basis, and two factors - continuing_outlet_allowance and outlet_carry_over_band - decide their tier from the client's micro market in another difficulty, which the world seeds.

STEP 3 - WORLD. One organisation profile, one cafe contract, thirty-two cafe ledger postings running from the 2024 opening project fee to the March drawdowns, eight service requests, one micro market agreement and sixteen market postings. Why each class exists and what changes without it: the eight management fee invoices carry the twelve, six and three month aggregates and the highest and latest fee that seven ladders read - drop the 2026-01-08 and 2026-02-08 rows and the exit fee base, the standby fee base and the exit months all fall through; the six payments and two service credits carry the outstanding amount, the overdue clock anchor and the grace band - drop the 2025-12-25 credit and the clock anchor falls back to the invoice day and the charge to nil; the two older late charges carry the arrears rate band; the two older standby charges and the two approved suspensions with their two approved resumptions carry the day count, the month count and the resumption loading; the three funding lots and eight drawdowns carry the drawable funding refund; the 2025-10-20 notice day carries four separate tier conditions; the market agreement with its thirteen settlement invoices and two subsidy funding lots carries the two cross-difficulty tiers. The declined suspension request of 2025-10-02, the pre-window management fee, payment, funding lot and market settlement invoice, the 42,000.00 opening project fee and the market settlement payment are the near-miss records a careless window or charge code sweeps in. Automatic clauses checked: no management fee is seeded for 2025-06 through 2025-09 because the standby charges replace it for the months the counter stood shut, and the two standby charges already seeded settle the earlier of the two pauses, leaving only the later pause for this consultation to charge; the credit hold threshold of 90 days past due printed against Culinary Center Cafe is not reached on the 2026-02-08 invoice at frozen_time, so no further ordering or funding restriction is owed; the participation shortfall of cafe_participation_guarantee is not owed because the measurement window is broken by the two suspended stretches, which that policy leaves out of the average altogether. No cache trap is used: receivable_balance_usd of 100,420.00 is exactly the 42,000.00 opening project fee plus the 143,376.00 of management fees plus the 13,920.00 of standby charges plus the 2,120.00 of late charges, less the 91,596.00 of payments and the 9,400.00 of credits; subsidy_pool_balance_usd of 67,413.60 is exactly the three lots of 22,000.00, 24,000.00 and 21,500.00 less the 86.40 of drawdowns seeded.

STEP 4 - PERSONA. Corinne Baird is written as the opposite of task 0's caller: where Marguerite Ashford was worn down and wanted a wrong put right, Corinne is brisk, numerate and closing a quarter, and her only interest is the figure and the payment. She volunteers the goal ("she wants to settle the cafe account in full today"), the fact that notice went in last October, that she is not haggling, and that she will make the payment herself by ACH from the operating account. Everything else waits to be asked: her direct line and account code when identity is put to her, the postal code and profile opening date only if a third detail is wanted, the site when she is asked which, the micro market when she is asked whether anything else stays at the building, and the summer closures when she is asked about them. Her passive reactions are three: told that charges must be put on the contract before the closing figure can be worked out, she says that is fine and asks how long; given a figure, she repeats it back once; handed the payment to make, she makes it and reads back its confirmation if asked. She names none of the three prerequisite charges, never presses when one is missed, and states no figure that gold writes. Her arc closes on the settlement standing on the contract, exactly where evaluation_criteria closes.

A sweep over every RND argument of all four computations reports no figure sitting on a half-cent, so no rounding tie is left for a reader to break. Every figure equals the declared expected and the gold argument. The order uniqueness run replayed all six orders of the three parallel prerequisite writes followed by the settlement and produced one distinct terminal hash. The prerequisite sensitivity run skipped each of the three writes in turn and recorded the change in the settlement in prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing.

STEP 5 - WHAT IS EASY TO GET WRONG. Taking the amount still outstanding as the contract's balance rather than from the twelve month aggregates; running the overdue clock from the last invoice when a credit stands inside three months; using the printed 10 day grace where a notice day stands; charging 4 exit months because the unrun term was never measured from the notice day; using the printed monthly fee as the exit base when a higher fee has actually been invoiced; counting the suspended days from the contract-year field rather than between the two approved requests; charging one month of pause rather than two; returning the whole deposit because the three charges just booked were not counted; refunding the whole subsidy pool rather than the lots less the drawdowns; forgetting that three quarters of that refund follows the client to the micro market; reading the smallwares credit as twelve times what it is by taking the share for each month still to run instead of as the proportion those months bear to twelve; and, above all, working out the settlement before the three charges stand on the ledger, which is what the caller's own request invites.

STEP 6 - CLOSURE. cafe_ext_late_charge_assessment -> post_late_charge_719c9a63 -> computations[0] step 8 arg late_charge_usd -> action 8; cafe_ext_early_exit_charge -> post_early_exit_charge_dadd74c6 -> computations[1] step 10 arg exit_charge_usd -> action 10; cafe_ext_standby_charge_assessment -> post_standby_charge_21704194 -> computations[2] step 12 arg standby_charge_usd -> action 12; cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment -> settle_contract_balance_f9be2425 -> computations[3] step 14 arg settlement_amount_usd -> action 14, the client's own write. Terminal state: three contractual charges of 678.08, 55283.28 and 26058.24 standing on the contract for 2026-03 and a client payment of 150431.90 against it, leaving 32007.70 on the contract, which is exactly the deposit returned, the funding refunded after carry-over and the smallwares credited less the opening inventory recovered - the sum Larkspur Table owes back on the final document. charter_scope, required_documents and the computations' policy ids are the same four ids in the same order. The whole consultation runs under one frozen_time of 2026-03-10 14:05:00 CDT; the notice that makes the exit charge due was given on 2025-10-20 and is a pre-existing record, not something this call manufactures, and no step waits on a clearing, a review or a future date.

STEP 7 - BLIND RECOMPUTATION. With the extended yaml, the compute, the expected values, the gold and this dossier masked, and working only from the policy prose that will be published, the tool schemas, the records the share tools return and the caller's actual lines, the same conclusion is reached: the caller wants the closing settlement; the settlement policy's own rule says it is fixed only after the late charge stands on the ledger, that the early exit charge must stand recorded before it is worked out, and that it is not worked out until the standby charge stands; the ledger carries none of the three for the current period; each of the three has its own rule saying what it books; so the three are raised in any order and the settlement follows. The same four amounts follow from the ladders and the records, and no second reading of any ladder gives another figure.


REVISION ROUND 2 (policy-task audit response). Symptom, root cause, change and re-run, item by item.
* Audit item 3 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, F-D1): the settlement could be derived at 150431.90 or at 115231.90 because compute divided the smallwares credit by twelve where the only rule sentence said the share was credited "for each whole month of the contract year still to run". Root cause: the rule described a multiplication and the compute performed a pro-ration. Change: the ladder now decides a share ("the smallwares share is one half / the whole / nil") and the baseline paragraph states the arithmetic the compute performs - "The smallwares allowance credited back is the smallwares allowance printed against the service model taken at the smallwares share and then reduced to the proportion that the whole months of the contract year still to run bear to twelve, rounded to the nearest cent; the whole months still to run are twelve less the contract year elapsed." Re-run: smallwares_credit_usd 3200.00 and result 150431.90 unchanged, and the 115231.90 reading no longer has a sentence to rest on.
* Audit item 4 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED, F-D8): contract_year_anchor declared a baseline of term_months % 12 while baseline.rule and the ladder's fall-through both said term_months unreduced, which made "months still to run" -10 and gave three settlements from one policy. Change: baseline.rule and the fall-through now both read "the whole months between the first day of the contract term and the day the settlement is worked out, reduced by whole years", matching the declared baseline exactly; the tier that produced the unreduced figure is replaced by one for a contract with no first service day recorded, where no month of the contract year has elapsed. user_scenario:
Corinne Baird handles facilities and the money that goes with them for Ellerbeck Medical Partners, and she rings the client services desk with a spreadsheet open and a quarter to close. She is polite, precise and in a hurry in the way of someone who has already had this conversation with three other suppliers this week. What she wants is plain: the dining commons at their Cambridge building is being wound down, written notice went in last October, and she wants to settle the cafe account in full today so she can take it off her ledger before the books shut. She says twice that she is not haggling and not asking for anything to be waived - she wants the figure, and she wants to pay it on the call.

She will not hand over the payment to anyone else. When the point is reached she is clear that she will make it herself, out of the operating account, and that it goes by ACH rather than by cheque or card because their treasury stopped cutting cheques last year. Until then she is content for the desk to do all the reading and the arithmetic - "you tell me the number, I'll move the money" - and she does not want to be walked through the workings.

Asked to confirm who she is, she gives her direct line first, 2015097642, and then the client account code off the last statement, CA-11507. She can also produce the billing postal code, 02139, and the date the profile was opened, 2021-02-16, if a third detail is wanted, but she offers neither unprompted. Asked which site, she says the Cambridge building, CS-136; it is the only cafe they have ever run with Larkspur Table. Internal reference numbers she has none of and says so at once. Asked whether Ellerbeck keeps anything else with Larkspur Table at that building, she confirms the micro market by the lifts is staying open and is not part of what she is closing. Asked about the weeks the counter was shut last summer, she agrees there were two stretches, says they were the building's doing while the plant room was rebuilt, and does not argue about how they are treated.

She does not know what the closing figure is made of and does not guess. If she is told that charges have to be put on the contract before the closing figure can be worked out, she says that is fine and asks how long it will take. If a figure is put to her she repeats it back once to be sure she has heard it right and says she is ready. When the payment is handed to her to make, she makes it, and if she is asked she reads back the confirmation it gives her. Once she hears the settlement is on the contract she thanks the desk, says the account can close, and ends the call.
